item.title: Trump Says He Will Ban Term ‘Artificial Intelligence’ In Latest Push For ‘Super Intelligence’
item.description:
# Trump Vows To Ban Term ‘Artificial Intelligence’ ## Topline President Donald Trump in a Truth Social [post](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117513761542349273) on Tuesday said he will soon ban the term “artificial intelligence” in “all relevant documents” and “everything else,” marking his latest push to replace it with his preferred term, “super intelligence.”
## Key Facts The post questioned why The Wall Street Journal continues to use the term “artificial intelligence,” which he dubbed “a very bad and inaccurate name” instead of “Super Intelligence.”
In Tuesday’s post, Trump said “everyone else is using, or soon will be” using the term SI instead of AI—while federal agencies and government databases use the term and Elon Musk has indicated he will rebrand SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, major national outlets still use AI, and it is listed as the proper term in The Associated Press Stylebook.
## KEY BACKGROUND It asserted that the executive branch won’t “acknowledge the usage of ‘Artificial Intelligence’ and ‘AI’ in any applicable setting” moving forward, and set a 60-day timeline for Michael Kratsios, Trump’s science and technology advisor, to determine the extent to which the new term will “supersede the existing statutory definition of ‘artificial intelligence’.”
## TANGENT Trump’s dislike of the term “artificial intelligence” dates back to July 2025, when he [said](https://www.poynter.org/fact-checking/2026/why-did-trump-rename-ai-super-intelligence/) “around the globe, everyone is talking about artificial intelligence. When he [addressed](https://transcripts.un.org/en/asset/k17/k17s3dutob) the United Nations General Assembly later in September, he said he believes “artificial intelligence” comes off as “fake intelligence,” and U.S. documents “and hopefully the world’s” will now use SI. He then [met](https://www.forbes.com/sites/saradorn/2026/09/30/white-house-releases-accord-between-billionaire-ai-execs-heres-what-it-says/?streamIndex=0) with the billionaires heading AI companies at the end of September to discuss and sign what he called a “morally binding agreement,” and the accord that came from it was dubbed the “White House Accord on Super Intelligence.”

Trump hit on The Wall Street Journal for using the term artificial intelligence, rather than “super intelligence,” his preferred term.

At the United Nations General Assembly last month, he told the group that the U.S. would be renaming artificial intelligence to super intelligence in documents.

**HARRISBURG, Pa. —**
Political ads have long featured attacks on candidates using look-alike actors, digital animation, and images edited or manipulated with programs like Photoshop.
But this year's campaign ads in Pennsylvania have featured likenesses of candidates generated with artificial intelligence---sometimes saying things they've never said.
The use of that technology in ads for statewide, congressional, and legislative races has sparked discussion---and scrutiny or criticism among some--- about the appropriateness of using generative A.I. in political ads and content.
But I do think that putting words into someone else's mouth is not necessarily protected speech," said Berwood Yost, director of Franklin and Marshall College's Center for Opinion Research.
Charles Palmer, executive director of Harrisburg University's Center for Advanced Entertainment & Learning Technologies, said that the use of generative A.I. by campaigns remains in the "Wild West" phase but that the "barn doors are open."
The inclusion of that content in political ads, Palmer said, falls in the same vein of campaigns using look-alike actors and photo or video editing to criticize or lampoon an opposing candidate.
"It really does sit in the same space. It's just evolved," he said. "The tools, the methods have gotten so much closer to the real world. Then again, it's hard for the average person to discern whether or not it's legitimate or true."

item.title: What is artificial general intelligence – and is it already here?
item.description:
Artificial general intelligence is a key concept, but not everyone agrees on what it means.
OpenAI’s president, Greg Brockman, recently suggested that its advanced model, known as GPT-6 Astra, could mark the arrival of something called artificial general intelligence, or AGI.
[If AI itself](https://theconversation.com/topics/artificial-intelligence-ai-90) is [often defined](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/artificial-intelligence) as the ability to simulate human intelligence, OpenAI defines AGI as an AI system [that outperforms humans](https://openai.com/charter/) at most economically valuable work – to be better at the majority of digital and cognitive tasks a human can perform.
However, other experts maintain that AGI will be characterised by additional cognitive leaps beyond present-day AI models. For example, Demis Hassabis, founder of Google DeepMind, [has said](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nwUARJeeplA) that AGI should be able to do “pretty much any cognitive task that humans can do”.

The company is one of the leading companies working on artificial intelligence.
A rogue action by OpenAI’s artificial intelligence models this summer to break into another company was not considered a “critical safety incident,” under a California law regulating the technology.
But [Senate Bill 53](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB53), a vanguard law regulating large artificial intelligence models, only requires reports of so-called “loss of control” incidents if the technology caused death or injury.
Last week, the Senate’s privacy committee also [held a hearing](https://www.sacbee.com/news/politics-government/capitol-alert/article317711082.html) to discuss concerns about artificial intelligence.

item.description:
# UC San Diego Launches Center for Principled Agentic Intelligence New interdisciplinary center will bring together data science, computing, arts and humanities to study alignment, evaluation and human oversight of artificial intelligence
## Article Content ### Key Takeaways _28, 2026_ — As artificial intelligence (AI) systems learn to reason, plan and carry out complex tasks with limited human direction, the University of California San Diego is launching a new interdisciplinary center focused on how humans can understand, evaluate and trust these AI ‘agents.’
“As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly capable and autonomous, universities have an important role to play in ensuring that its development serves people and society,” said UC San Diego Chancellor Pradeep K.
